contents.text: وكتبته وكتبنا الجواب

يا مهديا نظما بديعا وقد ترجمه من غير الغناء / بنوره [?] يا سيدي نهتدي لحله من بعد اخفاء / ان الذي العزت [?] في مسجد وقاده الاطباء ق [?] للرآي [?] / فتجلى الالغاز اذ ترجمت يشهد للحاضر والنائي / وثانيها

contents.word_groups: about 20 (2-3 dotted dividers per line; not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: not stated on this page; the block is introduced by 'wa-thaniha' (and the second of them), so it is the second cipher of a pair/series begun on the previous page

correspondents.arabic: (no name on this page; 'wa-katabtuhu wa-katabna al-jawab' = I wrote to him and we wrote the reply, addressee presumably on previous page)

technique_remarks: none on this page; a verse praising an 'ingenious composition' (nazm badi') whose decipherment ('hall') is made known after concealment ('ikhfa'), 'al-algaz' (riddles) 'when translated' - reading uncertain
plaintext_for: no plaintext on this page; cipher block (7 lines) is 'wa-thaniha' (the second), presumably answered on f. 19v/20r; the preceding verse is the first cipher's answer or cover verse from previous page
certainty: low for the Arabic (stain top-left, several words guessed from distorted letters), medium for the cipher layout; sign counts approximate

contents.direction_remark: none stated; appears to continue the 'wa-thaniha' block that began on f. 19r (no text between the two cipher parts), so one block of about 14 lines

contents.text: فحللته سريعا فوجدته / حبيبي وجهه قمرا اذا ما تبدى خلته بدرا تماما / دعا نصف اسمه لي ثم ابدى الى نصفه الثاني ملاما [reading of some words uncertain] / ومدد شددت ثانية [?] وحذف لرابع نفى عني المناما [?] / واكسبني قبيل الفجر هما وبعد العصر اعطاني ذماما
وكتبنا الجواب

technique_remarks: verses read as a name riddle (half of the name, extend/double a letter 'madd shaddat thaniya', delete for the fourth) - not certain; 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an fa-wajadtuhu' = I solved it quickly and found it
plaintext_for: block of 7 lines on this page together with the 7 lines on previous page f. 19r
certainty: medium for the layout, low for the verse words (stain, closely written); the plaintext is verse, not a letter, and I did not match it to the signs

contents.text: الى من ارسل لنظم انسجاما وترجم لغزه اهدي سلاما / سلام مقصر في حل لغز وحل مترجم ابدي نظاما [?] / وما شيء يراه الناس علما علاه الا وكنت به اماما [?] / لبسناد [?] ملجاحر [?] زاد دواء لشدة دمل يشفي السقاما [?] / قوله قبيل الفجر وبعد العصر من انواع الايهام وقوله / عن الدملج وجهه قمر من احسن الاستعارات مرشحا / بقوله بدرا تماما   وثالث المترجمات

contents.direction_remark: none stated; introduced as 'wa-thalith al-mutarjimat' (the third of the translated ones)

correspondents.arabic: الى من ارسل لنظم (verse addressed 'to him who sent the poem'; no name)

technique_remarks: lines 5-7 are the compiler's comment on the preceding riddle verse: 'qawluhu qubayl al-fajr wa-ba'd al-'asr min anwa' al-ihham' (his saying 'before dawn and after afternoon' is one of the kinds of ambiguity/ihham) and 'wajhuhu qamar ... min ahsan al-isti'arat murashshahan bi-qawlihi badran tamman' (face a moon, one of the best metaphors, strengthened by 'a full moon'); so the previous block was a riddle on a name by verse; the answer was by the compiler (verses lines 1-4, a reply to the sender)
plaintext_for: lines 1-7 answer/comment on the blocks of ff. 19r-19v; the cipher block on this page (third mutarjim) has its plaintext on f. 20v or later
certainty: medium for lines 1-2 and 5-7, low for lines 3-4; worm marks and stain near line 1-3

contents.word_groups: about 40 (3-4 dividers per line, not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated; continues the third translated block ('wa-thalith al-mutarjimat') begun on f. 20r (6 lines there), so the block is at least 18 lines. A lone dotted divider stands alone in the lower left after the last line (line 13 position), i.e. the block may continue overleaf

technique_remarks: none on this page; sign shapes differ from the previous block (many teardrop/ring-shaped signs, e.g. a closed loop sign very frequent)
plaintext_for: block on this page continues the block of previous page f. 20r; no plaintext on this page
certainty: high for layout, approximate sign counts; the page has no Arabic text, margin shows through bleed from the next leaf

contents.direction_remark: none stated; the sign shapes here (numeral-like 4, 7, 8, a triangle-over-bars sign, a hook sign) differ from the ring/teardrop signs of f. 20v, so this looks like a new block or an alphabet change; the link to the 20v block is unclear

contents.text: فحللته سريعا لسهولته وهو / ولينة الاعطاف واسعة الاكناف وطيبها / مباح على انها تجافاها اهل الصلاح تزور / اذا جن الليل وترحل عند الصباح توهمها / العسى [?] وتطعنها الاسنة وهي معدودة من / نعيم اهل الجنة وجمعها يستر بالظهور وافتراشها / بعقد جايز غير محذور وخمد [?] منها ما يذم في / المذاهب وظهرها او [?] ظهر للراكبان جمالها

technique_remarks: 'fa-halaltuhu sari'an li-suhulatihi wa-huwa' = I solved it quickly because of its easiness, and it is ... ; the plaintext reads as a rhyming-prose riddle description of some object (soft, wide, lawful but shunned by the pious, visited at night, leaves at dawn, counted among the delights of Paradise, spread out as a bed) - object not identified by me; not a letter
plaintext_for: block of 5 lines on this page (the 20v block of 12 lines, 20r block of 6 lines have no plaintext of their own that I could identify; possibly this plaintext answers one or all of them)
certainty: medium for the layout; low-medium for the Arabic words (dense, some join errors); sign counts approximate

contents.text: ربها جملته وازدها نعمه فاذكر اسم ربك / حين تاوي اليها واشكر نعمة ربك اذا استوت بك عليها [first word of line 1 and some words uncertain]
وكتبت الجواب

جوابها مذكور في سورة الواقعة التي هي للفقر / عن قارئها دافعة فقيل اصحاب اليمين لثانية / ومنها الثمين والدانية ضمنها قطن مندوف / ويحتمل ان تجعل من صوف وربما كان فيها التصاوير / فيحمد ان تداس للتحقير واحسن ما كانت على / الاريك وقد يعبر بها عن النساء العوانك فالحقيقة / نحسنها المجاز كما حسنت المترجمات الالغاز / وهذا احرز الكلام بعد اهل السلام والسلم والحضر[?] / بي الشيخ بدر الدين المذكور ايضا مترجما فقال لك [reading of last lines uncertain]

correspondents.translit: al-Shaykh Badr al-Din (the aforementioned); he 'also, in cipher, said to you' - probably the correspondent/setter of the cipher verses on ff. 19-21; no patronymic given on this page

technique_remarks: 'jawabuha madhkur fi surat al-Waqi'a' = its answer is mentioned in sura al-Waqi'a (Q 56, 'and raised couches/furush marfu'a'); the answer to the riddle is thus beds/carpets (furush, 'wa-furushin marfu'a'); the following lines describe the object (cotton-filled, could be of wool, may carry pictures, best on couches, metaphorically women) and say 'as ciphers adorn riddles (al-mutarjimat al-alghaz)'; no cipher mechanics
plaintext_for: gloss/solution of the riddle prose on f. 21r; no cipher block on this page
certainty: medium for most lines, low for lines 11-13 and for the first line (tight writing, some letter joins unclear). The Quranic reference is read from 'surat al-waqi'a'; I did not check the sura text

contents.word_groups: about 35-40 (3-4 dividers per line, not counted exactly)
contents.direction_remark: none stated on this page. Introduced by the last line of f. 21v ('al-Shaykh Badr al-Din ... ayDan mutarjiman fa-qala laka' = [he] also said to you in cipher), so the block is the verse/letter of Badr al-Din in cipher. New sign family: a hooked 'h'-shaped sign, a sign like 'H', a 'lam-alif'-like shape, hook-and-bar signs; different from the ring signs of f. 20v

plaintext_for: block on this page is the cipher announced at the end of previous page f. 21v; plaintext not on this page (look on f. 22v)
certainty: high for layout, sign counts approximate (+-2 per line); no Arabic text on this page; faint show-through from verso

contents.direction_remark: last line of the block of f. 22r (11 lines + this one = 12 lines), same sign family

contents.text: فحللته ووجدت اللام الف حرفا واحدا والتاء الاولى [?] / شكلا غير باقي الثاءات [?] سهوا والاثبات [?] (words of lines 2-3 partly uncertain)

تخالهم الحلم صما عن الخنا وخرسا عن الفحشاء عند التناثر / ومرضى اذا لاقوا اخيا وعفة وعند الحروب كالليوث [?] / هم عز انصاف وذل تواضع بهم ولهم ذلت رقاب المعاشر [?] الجوادر [?] / كان همو وصما خافون عارهو وما وصمهم الا انتقام المعابر [?]
وكتب السيد الشريف شهاب الدين احمد الحسيني الدمشقي

contents.word_groups: no dotted dividers visible in this block; groups not countable
contents.direction_remark: none stated; the signs here are distorted Arabic letter shapes and numerals (e.g. ghayn-like, lam-like, 7, 8, 3, 18), a different type of cipher from the invented signs above; the last line ends with '18'

contents.text: ابن علي ابن غنم [or غانم] الخطيب (written vertically in the right margin beside the cipher; reading of the third word uncertain)

correspondents.arabic: السيد الشريف شهاب الدين احمد الحسيني الدمشقي
correspondents.translit: al-Sayyid al-Sharif Shihab al-Din Ahmad al-Husayni al-Dimashqi (wrote the cipher below). Margin: Ibn 'Ali ibn Ghanim(?) al-Khatib

technique_remarks: 'fa-halaltuhu wa-wajadtu al-lam-alif harfan wahidan' = I solved it and found lam-alif to be one letter (one sign); 'wa-l-ta' al-ula shaklan ghayr baqi al-thaqat sahwan' (reading uncertain) = the first ta/tha is of different shape from the other ones, by oversight
plaintext_for: first cipher line is the end of the block on previous page f. 22r; the lines 2-7 are the solution note and the verses of that block. The 5-line block of signs at the bottom (after 'wa-kataba al-Sayyid al-Sharif Shihab al-Din') has no plaintext on this page
certainty: medium for text, low for lines 4-7 (verse words guessed in places); marginal name read from rotated crop

contents.direction_remark: last line of the letter-shaped cipher block begun on f. 22v (bottom, 5 lines + this line = 6 lines); signs are distorted Arabic letters/numerals (waw, sin, fa, 5, ha, dal, 8, 3)

contents.text: فحللته ووجدت اللام الف حرفا والهمزة غير الالف وقد حبط فيه وهو تغيير [?] في اصل وهو [?] / لبني قد بنيك من مخالفتي حذرا ولاجل ذلك قد اثبتك عذرا [?] / لبني لاخبار الشام لشوق والصوم عند وصول ذلك / فقد نذر [?]
وكتب لك [?]

contents.direction_remark: none stated; new sign family of wave-shaped and small closed-loop signs, different from the letter-shaped block above

correspondents.arabic: وكتب لك [? - name after it not on this page; the writer is probably the one named at the start of the next block]

technique_remarks: 'fa-halaltuhu wa-wajadtu al-lam alif harfan wa-l-hamza ghayr al-alif wa-qad habata fihi ...' = I solved it and found lam-alif to be one letter, and the hamza different from the alif; 'habata fihi' (he erred in it?) - reading uncertain. Lines 3-6 look like an apology/excuse (i'tidhar, 'udhr) concerning news from Syria (al-Sham), longing and fasting on arrival of that - words not secure
plaintext_for: the compiler's note (lines 2-7) belongs to the letter-shaped cipher block on f. 22v; the 5-line block of wave signs at the bottom has no plaintext on this page
certainty: low-medium for lines 2-8 (read from a crop at 2x; word joins and diacritics uncertain, several sentences not understood); high for layout

contents.direction_remark: continues the wave-sign block begun at the bottom of f. 23r (5 + 5 = 10 lines); same sign family; last line short (7 signs), so the block ends here

contents.text: فحللتها سريعا لسهولتها وهي للبحتري / الثلاث اللواتي لو اصيب بهن رضوى لاصبح منها [?] (واهي السبب - small insertion above line 8, reading uncertain) / حب [?] لال رسول الله اولة وثانيا اننى من اكرم العرب / ولا اشك ولا ارتاب ثالثه بانني ادركتني حرفة الادب / وكتب لي انسان من اهل الموصل بنا امتحانا

contents.direction_remark: new block (not yet its plaintext); signs: square-bracket, X, 5, 4, wave, hook shapes; introduced by 'wa-kataba li insan min ahl al-Mawsil bina imtihanan' = a man from the people of Mosul wrote to me testing us (in cipher)

correspondents.translit: insan min ahl al-Mawsil, 'a man from Mosul' - unnamed, wrote to test

technique_remarks: 'fa-halaltuha sari'an li-suhulatiha wa-hiya li-l-Buhturi' = I solved it quickly for its easiness, and it (the plaintext) is by al-Buhturi (the classical poet); the quoted verses mention love of the family of the Messenger of God first, being of the noblest Arabs second, and 'the hurt of the profession of letters (hirfat al-adab)' third, i.e. a poem about three things; the three-point structure is the 'thalath'
plaintext_for: lines 6-10 give the plaintext (quoted verses attributed to al-Buhturi) for the 5-line wave block on this page and f. 23r (10 lines). The 2-line block at the bottom has no plaintext on this page
certainty: medium for the layout, low-medium for the Arabic of lines 7-10 (attribution to al-Buhturi is the compiler's statement, I have not verified the verse)

contents.direction_remark: end of the 2-line block begun at the bottom of f. 23v (so that block = 3 lines); same sign family; the line continues with the Arabic word 'fa-fataha' at its left end

contents.text: ففتح الله تعالى بحله [?] سريعا مع غرابته وقلته وهو / [first word not read] لتعلما سر سعدى تجداني بسر سعدى شحيحا [?] / وكنا نعرف البيت ذكره الغزالي رحمه الله في / كتاب جواهر القرآن وكتب لي انسان من اهل اسنا [?] / يسمى نور الدين علي

contents.direction_remark: new block, no direction stated; sign family: // (double slash) sign frequent, square, triangle, 8, 9, T-shaped and cross-hatched signs; introduced by 'wa-kataba li insan min ahl [Isna?] yusamma Nur al-Din 'Ali'

correspondents.arabic: انسان من اهل اسنا [?] يسمى نور الدين علي
correspondents.translit: a man from the people of Isna(?) [place reading uncertain], called Nur al-Din 'Ali

technique_remarks: 'fa-fataha Allah ta'ala bi-hallihi sari'an ma'a gharabatihi wa-qillatihi' = God opened its solution quickly despite its strangeness and rareness (reading of bi-hallihi uncertain); the plaintext is a verse (...tu'lama sirra Su'da tajidani bi-sirri Su'da shahihan = 'if you two knew Su'da's secret you would find me miserly with Su'da's secret'); 'wa-kunna na'rif al-bayt dhakarahu al-Ghazali rahimahu llah fi kitab Jawahir al-Qur'an' = we knew the verse, al-Ghazali mentions it in Jawahir al-Qur'an (named authority: al-Ghazali)
plaintext_for: lines 1-6 give the plaintext (a verse) for the 3-line block that started on f. 23v bottom (the Mosul man's cipher), ended line 1 here. The 7-line block at the bottom of this page has no plaintext on this page
certainty: medium for lines 1-2 and 4-6 (read from a 2x crop), low for the first word of line 3 and the verse's exact wording; high for layout, sign counts approximate

contents.text: فحللت ذلك سريعا لسهولته وهو / مات من عاش بالفضيلة جوعا وحظي من يقود [?] ينسخر [?] / ورمينا بصرف دهر عجيب جلس النذل والكريم تاخر / وترجم لي المولى علم الدين ابن [?] كاتب سوق الخيل الموقع / بالباب الشريف

contents.direction_remark: none stated; letter-shaped signs (distorted Arabic letters: ayn/ghayn-like hooked sign very frequent, lam-alif-like, waw, fa, kaf, ta, sad, sin, ha, mim) separated by dotted dividers - a simple substitution of letter forms; introduced by the Arabic line 'wa-tarjama li al-mawla 'Alam al-Din ...' (the cipher is his)

contents.text: فحللتها في الحال بحضور من كتبها بالمدرسة القراسنقرية وهي [text breaks off; continues on next page]
not read: a few small marks/signs in the left margin beside the cipher (about 8 small characters, cipher-like, possibly show-through)

correspondents.arabic: المولى علم الدين ابن [?] كاتب سوق الخيل الموقع بالباب الشريف
correspondents.translit: al-Mawla 'Alam al-Din ibn [patronymic not read], katib suq al-khayl, al-muwaqqi' bi-l-bab al-sharif (secretary of the Horse Market, signatory/chancery clerk at the Noble Gate). The plaintext at the top of the page (verse about the noble starving while the base prosper) is the answer to the Nur al-Din 'Ali block of f. 24r

technique_remarks: 'fa-halaltu dhalika sari'an li-suhulatihi wa-huwa' = I solved that quickly because of its easiness, and it is [the verse]; 'fa-halaltuha fi al-hal bi-hudur man katabaha bi-l-madrasa al-Qarasunqūriyya wa-hiya...' = I solved it on the spot in the presence of the one who wrote it, at the Qarasunqur madrasa, and it is ... (the plaintext continues on the next page, f. 25r)
plaintext_for: lines 1-5 (verse 'mata man 'asha bi-l-fadila ju'an ...' = he died who lived on virtue in hunger ...) are the plaintext for the 7-line block at the bottom of the previous page f. 24r (Nur al-Din 'Ali's cipher). The 6-line letter-shaped block on this page is solved in lines 12-13 (in the presence of its writer at the Qarasunqur madrasa) and continues overleaf; its plaintext is not on this page
certainty: medium-high for lines 1-5 and 12-13 (read from crops), word 'ينسخر' and patronymic uncertain; high for layout; sign counts approximate (+-1). Possible bleed/fingerprint stain at right
